entities.name: Simón de Anda y Salazar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Simón de Anda y Salazar (1710–1776) was a Spanish colonial administrator who served as Governor-General of the Philippines (1770–1776) and is celebrated as the hero of Filipino resistance against the British occupation of Manila (1762–1764). When a British East India Company fleet captured Manila during the Seven Years' War, Anda escaped to the interior and organized a Filipino guerrilla resistance that kept Spanish authority alive outside Manila for the two years of British occupation. His resistance prevented the British conquest from becoming permanent — ensuring that Spain regained the Philippines in the 1763 Treaty of Paris.

His later governorship was notable for his conflicts with the Jesuits before their expulsion — Anda was a fierce opponent of Jesuit power in the Philippines.

He died in office in 1776.

He is celebrated as one of the greatest Filipino colonial heroes.
